imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: After the Books. Cast/design continuity: Two fictional children in a modest domestic courtyard: a girl with straight shoulder-length dark hair in faded clay-red clothes and a smaller dark-haired boy in blue-green clothes. Handmade cloth, a few worn books with blank unreadable pages, wooden threshold and stone ground. No national emblems or identifiable real portraits.. CELL 0: Wide modest courtyard. A girl kneels beside a low wooden chest and carefully tucks a handmade cloth over a small stack of worn books, both hands touching real cloth and paper. She looks toward an unseen doorway with concern. Keep the danger outside the frame and the setting quiet. CELL 1: Same courtyard. The girl draws the books toward her chest with both arms while the cloth falls across her knees. Her expression is alarmed but contained; no visible attacker, uniform, weapon or violence against a body. A loose blank page has lifted slightly in a breeze. CELL 2: A few books burn in a small restrained outdoor fire on bare stone, separated safely from people. The girl is seen at a distance with empty open hands and lowered shoulders. No body is harmed. Warm firelight is sparse; loss is not immediately covered by magical images. CELL 3: After the fire, the girl sits beside cold grey ash, empty hands resting on her knees. She lifts her face as a small pale abstract paper-like curve appears above her palm, suggesting a first remembered story without readable letters or restored books. The loss stays physically present. CELL 4: The smaller boy settles on the courtyard step a believable arm’s length from her. He leans forward with an attentive face; she turns toward him and begins a small open-hand storytelling gesture. Both are grounded on the stone step; no book lies between them. CELL 5: A small attentive circle of distinct children sits around the girl on the same step. She tells a story with one modest hand gesture; tiny faint imagined shapes appear only behind her, not as a replacement pile of books. Empty cloth and distant ash remain. Human listening carries the ending. Editorial limit: Book destruction is an object loss, not violence against people. Keep pages blank/unreadable; add no political insignia or unprovided action.
